request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A held person's claims, and held claims, now count in every total again: claimed, due-totals,
overdue, the period figures, backing, the rollup lines. The only thing a hold still does is in the
pools: a held person gets no cut and their share is spread over the others, as before.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored

AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Holds no longer take anything out of the totals. A held person's claims and held claims now count in claimed, due-totals, overdue, the period figures, backing and the rollup lines again. Pools work as before: a held person gets no cut, and their share is spread over the others. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 acceptance tests.

What changed:
- **Server:** in `Dues.java`, the rule that decides whether a claim is left out of the totals now only looks at retirement. It no longer checks the person's holds or the claim's own hold. Every total on the server goes through that one rule, so they all changed together. The pool cut code (`Pools.cut`) checks holds itself and wasn't touched.
- **Front end:** some figures are also worked out in the browser, and those skipped held claims too. I removed that from the period figures in `periods.ts` and the tag rollup in `tags.ts`, and deleted the `heldOut` helper in `claims.ts`, which nothing uses any more.
- **Comments:** I updated the code comments that said a hold keeps a claim out of the totals. One of those edits (in `ClaimService.java`) came after the passing test run. It's comment-only and the code still compiles.

Held claims still have their Hold/Release toggle and their audit records. A hold just doesn't change any figure except the pool cut.

probe.probe_text:
I changed no files. I read the due calculation myself (`claim/Dues.java`, `claim/Claim.java`, `ClaimStatus`, `rate/RateTable.java`). Four read-only sub-agents read the rest: claim services, person/period/access, sheet/rate/pool and the frontend. I haven't re-checked every line reference they gave. Server paths are under `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/`.

# 1. Figures and the rules that decide them

## A claim's figures
- **Shown as stored:** `amount`, `date`, `note`, `ref`, `tags`, `status`, `claim-number`, `openedBy`, `dueBy`, `corrects`, `splitFrom`, `settleBatch`, `lateEntry`, `waived`, `held`, `remindedOn`, `deferredUntil`, `proofs` (receipt/photo), `stated`.
- **Amount:** when the claim has lines, it is the lines added up, rounded half up (`Claim.addLine`). A negative amount makes the claim a **correction** (`isCorrection`).
- **Due:** `Dues.figure`, checked in this order:
  1. `settledDue` if the claim has been settled (frozen).
  2. `statedDue` if a statement binds it (`bound` = `isStated`) and `statedAsShown`.
  3. Otherwise `base`. That is the old-style stated figure, or else `rateFigure` = amount × rate in force on the claim's date for the person's grade then ÷ 100, `setScale(2, rounding)`.
     - The rate lookup is `RateTable.on`: the latest from-date on or before the date. An ended rate gives null and does not fall back to an earlier one. If the sheet has none, it tries parent sheets up to 3 levels, then the clone's source.
     - Forward-only rates apply only to claims added after the rate was saved (`Rate.appliesTo`, using `forwardAfter`).
  4. A correction stops at `base`: no floor, no late charge.
  5. Anything else is `floored` (the greater of the figure and the dated `floor`, default 1.00). If the claim is `overdue` and not `waived`, it gets `lateCharge` on top.
- **Late charge:** one step per full 30 days (`LATE_PERIOD_DAYS`) past `graceBy`. Each step adds `latePct` (as in force at that step's date) on figure plus charge so far, so it compounds. Each step is rounded.
- **Rounding:** `RateTable.rounding(roundsBy)`. The dated `rounding` setting wins if set. Otherwise half-up before `policyDate` (the sheet's today if none is set) and half-even on or after it. A correction rounds by the date of the claim it corrects (`getRoundsBy`).
- **Due "n/a":** shown when no rate is in force.
- **`dueBy`:** fixed when the claim is added. It is the `terms`-th business day after the claim's date, skipping weekends and holidays (`HolidayService.businessDaysAfter`).
  - Terms come from `termsFor`: the person's terms, else the grade's, else the sheet's (default 14), taken on the sheet's today.
  - Edit and redate never change it. Adding a holiday recomputes it for claims that are not SETTLED/VOID and whose due-by is on or after the holiday.
- **`overdue`:** OPEN or PENDING, not `deferred`, and `graceBy` (dueBy plus the grade's grace on the claim's date) is before today.
- **`deferred`:** OPEN and today is before `deferredUntil`.
- **`reviewLate`:** in REVIEW, with `reviewOn` plus `reviewSla` before today.
- **Numbers:** given on open (or on review), never reused, never given to drafts. A voided claim keeps its number.
  - Normally the number is `<FY>-<n>`, the fiscal year of the due-by. One sequence is shared across the whole tree of sheets.
  - From `periodNumberingFrom` on, it is `<period>-<n>`, or `X-<n>` when no period contains the due-by.
  - Reassign, transfer and clone renumber (`renumber`, `numberArrived`) and retire the old number.
- **`claim-period`:** worked out in the browser as the period containing `dueBy`.

## Statuses (`ClaimStatus`)
- The flow is DRAFT → OPEN, or → REVIEW if the due is above `reviewThreshold`. From OPEN a claim goes to SETTLED, or to PENDING when a clerk settles above the clerk limit. PENDING is approved (SETTLED) or rejected (back to OPEN).
- VOID is allowed from DRAFT, OPEN, PENDING or REVIEW. A SETTLED claim can be voided only by a steward within 7 days of settling.
- A DRAFT can be DELETED, and restored only on the same sheet today.
- `counts()` = OPEN, PENDING or SETTLED. `unpaid()` = OPEN or PENDING.

## A person's figures (`PersonController.PersonView.of` → `Dues`)
- **Which claims count** (`Dues.counts`): status counts, not deferred, and not `retiredOut`. `retiredOut` means unbound, OPEN or PENDING, and today has reached `retiredFrom`.
  - **A hold changes no total.** A held claim or held person still counts everywhere. The only effect of a person's hold is that they get no pool cut. The comments in `PersonService.hold` and `PeriodService.close` say otherwise; the code wins.
- **`claimed`:** the sum of *amounts* of the claims that count, leaving out corrections.
- **`dueTotal`:** `capped(uncapped)`.
  - `uncapped` is the sum of the counting claims' figures.
  - It is null (n/a) when today's grade has no current rate, unless some claim keeps its figure anyway (settled, bound, another grade's rate, or the rate has ended).
  - The cap in force today limits it. `excess` is what is over the cap.
- **`settledTotal` / `openTotal`:** the uncapped sum split into SETTLED versus OPEN+PENDING.
- **`overdueCount` / `overdueTotal`:** claims that count and are overdue.
- **`aged0to30` / `aged31to60` / `aged61`:** the due of OPEN/PENDING counting claims, grouped by age from the claim's date. A future-dated claim is age 0.
- **`active`:** has an OPEN or PENDING counting claim dated within the last 30 days, today included.
- **`recentSettled`:** the `settledDue` of SETTLED claims dated within the last 90 days.
- **Grade and terms:** `grade` = `gradeOn(today)` and `terms` = `termsOn(today)`, each the latest dated entry on or before today.
- **Retirement:** `retired` means a `retiredFrom` is set; `retiredNow` means today has reached it.
- **Other flags:** `held` means any hold exists, whatever its dates. `flag` is shown while today is on or before `flagUntil`. Also shown: `approver`, `origin`/`arrivedOn` (set by a transfer), `clashing` (name or alias used elsewhere in the sheet tree), `tags`, `position`.
- **Statements:** `statementCount`, `statedTotal`, `statementDate`.
  - Taking a statement binds each counting claim to its figure as shown, late charge included. That freezes it until the claim is settled or released.
  - Cancelling a statement (steward only) releases *every* stated claim. Earlier bindings are not restored.
- **Computed only in the browser** (`people.ts`, `periods.ts`):
  - `person-backing`: each patron's `recentSettled` × their share. Shares split 100 equally, rounded half to even, with the remainder to the first patron.
  - `person-cut-total`: the person's pool cuts added up.
  - Live `person-period-*-due-total` and `-carried`.

## Sheet-level totals
- **On the server** (`Rollup`): due-total and overdue-total use `trimmedSum`, which drops the single highest and lowest figure when there are 3 or more. Claimed-total is a plain sum. An `ALERT` audit line is written when a person's due-total rises above `alertThreshold`.
- **Repeated in the browser** (in integer cents, `Math.round`): the header and rollup totals, the "my" and crew totals, the consolidated figures across child sheets, the summary by grade, period, month and void reason, and tag totals.

## Who may do what
- **Roles:** CLERK (the default), STEWARD, VIEWER.
  - A delegation covering today makes the user a steward, overriding even VIEWER.
  - Only a steward by role (not by delegation) may delegate.
- **Viewers and archived sheets:** `ViewerGuard` refuses every non-GET for a viewer, or for anyone on an archived sheet. Exceptions: `/load`, `/bulk-*` (which return 0 themselves), `/people/grade`, `/people/retire`, and `/plans/generate` for viewers.
- **Configurable permissions:** `Permission` covers OPEN, SETTLE, VOID and CLOSE (clerk and steward by default) and REASSIGN and REOPEN (steward only by default).
- **Steward only:** review, waive, resettle, redate, void a SETTLED claim, merge, transfer and undo, archive, clone, flag, lock a period, cancel a statement. Only a steward may open claims of a flagged person.
- **Four-eyes:** neither the opener nor the last editor may settle, part-settle or approve. Reject has no such check.
- **Approve / reject a PENDING claim:** a steward or the person's `approver`.
- **Clerk limit** (`canSettle`): uses `clerkLimitFor(grade on today, today)`. A clerk settling above it leaves the claim PENDING.
- **Proof:** above `proofThreshold`, a claim needs at least one proof of each kind in `proofKinds` before it can be settled.
- **Note:** above `noteThreshold`, a claim needs a note before it can be opened.
- **Not checked at all:** setting roles and settings, hold, retire, defer, approver.

## What dates decide
- **The sheet's `today`:**
  - It decides lateness and the late charge, deferral, the cap, the current grade and terms, the clerk-limit grade, retirement, flags, the 7-day void window, and the restore day.
  - It also sets the log dates and `reviewOn`.
  - Changing it records snapshots (`SheetPasts` and `DayEnds`), releases every editor lock, and auto-closes periods whose to-date plus `graceDays` has passed.
- **The claim's date:** the rate, the grade, grace, floor, rounding, and the note, review and proof thresholds.
- **The due-by:** which period the claim belongs to (closed or soft-closed, cap, numbering).
- **`entryDate`:** the default date for a new claim, via `claimDate`. Edit defaults to today instead.
- **`policyDate`:** switches rounding from half-up to half-even.
- **As-of view** (`X-As-Of` header): shows the sheet as it was on that day and refuses every change.

## Periods
- **`requireOpen`:** refuses any claim change whose **due-by** falls in a closed period. Comment, waive and remind skip this check.
- **Soft-closed:** changes are still allowed, but a claim added into it is marked `lateEntry` and a `LATE_ENTRY` audit line is written.
- **`cap`:** opening a claim is refused when the person already has that many unpaid claims due in the period.
- **Closing (`fix`) freezes three figures:**
  - `personTotals`: the claims due in the period whose status at the end of its last day counts.
  - `personCarried`: unpaid claims from earlier periods at their current figure, plus `personOpenings`.
  - `closedTotal`.
- **`reopen`:** steward only, and not while `locked`. It clears the frozen figures and keeps the openings.

## Imports, pastes and bulk actions
- **Paste claims** (`name,amount,date,note #ref`):
  - All or nothing; no negative amounts.
  - A line matching an existing DRAFT (same person, date and note) updates its amount; a line matching only non-drafts is refused.
  - Every line is then opened, so all the open rules apply. The count is every non-blank line.
- **Person import:** adds a new name or updates the person who has that name or alias. All or nothing. Returns added and updated.
- **Rate import and opening import:** all or nothing; return the line count.
  - An opening added to a closed period does not change its frozen carried figure until the period is reopened and closed again.
- **Bulk settle:** all or nothing, under one `settleBatch`. A claim left PENDING counts as settled.
- **Other bulk actions:** open, void, redate and reassign count each claim separately.

# 2. How hard it was to follow

It is not in one place a new developer could pick up. The core due maths in `Dues` and `RateTable` is reasonably contained. Everything around it is spread across a 1,200-line `ClaimService` with copied checks, the URL-matching `ViewerGuard`, ad-hoc role checks (some through `Permission`, some hard-coded to steward, some missing), settings split between sheet columns and dated rows, two snapshot systems, and frontend totals that repeat server logic in different rounding. Several comments contradict the code (holds, cap status, edit's default date, a split part's terms), so you have to trace the code itself to be sure.
